title: Corn Downy Mildew: How to Spot It and Protect Your Mais
metaTitle: Corn Downy Mildew: Signs, Damage and Control in Mais
metaDescription: Corn downy mildew shows as pale stripes and white fuzz on young mais, and it can wipe out a stand. Learn the signs and the steps that protect your corn.
excerpt: Corn downy mildew is the disease behind pale, striped, stunted mais seedlings with white fuzz on the leaves. In the Philippines, Peronosclerospora philippinensis causes it. It is one of the main diseases that can destroy a young corn stand.

blocks.text:
Peronosclerospora philippinensis, a water mold that behaves like a fungus, causes corn downy mildew. It attacks corn, and the disease is most common in warm, humid regions and in fields that flood. Researchers at the University of the Philippines Los Baños test corn lines against it. Breeding for resistance has been hard.

It matters because young plants are the most open to attack. A field can lose plants before it forms a crop. In severe cases, research papers report yield loss up to total loss. Our guide to [corn seeds](/crops/corn-seeds) and the page on [planting corn](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais) help you choose seed and plan around wet weeks.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: Leaves, the whole plant and panicles and ears
Corn downy mildew hits young corn most, in the first weeks after emergence, and it grows fastest in warm, humid weather and in fields that flood.

The fungus like organism makes spores on the leaf at night in humid air, and wind carries them to nearby corn. The Philippine species spreads from plant to plant by these spores and has no insect vector.

blocks.text: How to Identify Corn Downy Mildew

Look at the first true leaves of seedlings. The first sign is chlorotic stripes or a general yellowing. Early in the morning, check the underside of the leaf for a grayish white downy growth. Older infected plants have narrow, stiff, upright leaves, and their tassels come out malformed. Note that maize streak virus can hide the mildew symptoms. So check the leaf underside in the early morning, when the downy growth is easiest to see.

items: Pale or yellow stripes on the first true leaves of young seedlings.
A grayish white, downy growth on both sides of the leaf, easiest to see in the early morning.
Narrow, stiff and upright leaves that look dried out on older plants.
Stunted plants in patches, often in low areas that hold water.
Malformed tassels, little pollen, and ears that do not form or hold sterile seed.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Early stripes look like a nutrient problem or maize streak virus. A true downy mildew also shows grayish white fuzz on the leaf underside in the early morning. The plant stands stiff and narrow leaved.
How Corn Downy Mildew Hurts Your Corn

Researchers rate Peronosclerospora downy mildews a major constraint on corn production. Research papers report yield loss up to 100 percent in severe attacks. How bad it gets depends on the variety, the weather and how early infection strikes the plant. Plants hit at the seedling stage seldom give any ear.

There is no set spray threshold. Because the damage begins in the first weeks, the plan must be in place before sowing. Pick a tolerant variety, treat the seed and avoid low, wet ground. Planting corn again in the same field after a wet season? Check our guide on [crop pests in the Philippines](/pests/crop-pests-philippines). See our overview of [plant diseases in the Philippines](/diseases/plant-diseases-philippines) too.
How to Control Corn Downy Mildew

items: Plant a resistant or tolerant variety where one is sold. UPLB trials found some inbred lines with a high level of resistance, and your seed supplier or local agriculture office can say what suits your area.
Avoid fields that flood or hold water, and improve drainage before planting.
Walk the field in the first weeks, early in the morning, and pull and destroy infected seedlings right away.
Plant on time with your neighbors so that young corn does not stand beside older infected corn.
Clear grassy weeds and volunteer corn from the field and the bunds.
Treat the seed with a fungicide when the variety is not resistant, as the East West Seed plant doctor page advises.

blocks.text: Seed treatment is the usual first step against downy mildew. Researchers report that the Philippine pathogen can develop resistance to metalaxyl. So growers often use a mixture. Follow the FPA registered label.

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different fungicide group next time, so the disease does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to plant diseases](/diseases/plant-diseases-philippines) explains how.

items: Choose a downy mildew tolerant variety first, and ask your supplier for the latest list.
Treat seed before sowing in fields with a history of the disease.
Do not plant corn in low, flood prone spots during the wet season.
Keep records of which lots had the disease and move your corn away from them if you can.

blocks.text: Questions Farmers Ask About Corn Downy Mildew

items.q: What does corn downy mildew look like?
items.a: Young plants show pale stripes or yellowing on the first true leaves. Then a grayish white downy growth appears on the leaf. Later the leaves turn narrow and upright and the tassels come out malformed.

items.q: Can corn downy mildew kill my whole field?
items.a: In a severe attack it can, and research papers report losses up to 100 percent. Plants infected as seedlings seldom make an ear, so protect the crop in the first weeks.

items.q: Does metalaxyl still work against it?
items.a: Not always. Researchers report that Philippine downy mildew can develop resistance to metalaxyl. So growers often use a mixture and a resistant variety. Read more on [corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust) and other corn diseases too.
